summary: When the invoices list is empty, the page now says "No invoices match this filter" instead of drawing a table with headings and nothing under them.
Why: a header row over an empty body reads like the page is broken; it does not tell a person that their filter simply matched nothing.
What someone would notice: nothing, on today's data — the five seeded invoices render pixel-for-pixel as before. The message only appears once the list is empty.

blocks.caption: The empty state, reached by temporarily emptying the seed in lib/invoices.ts: the message sits exactly where the table was, with the same 1.5rem gap under the export button, and no <table> element is rendered at all. (That scratch edit was reverted and is not in this PR.)

The page on the repo's real data, after the change: the same five invoices, the same four columns, "Export 3 invoices as CSV" and "Total sent: $1,497.50". The table markup moved verbatim, so this screen is unchanged.

focus.title: The table markup moved verbatim, so the rendered DOM is byte-identical on non-empty data
focus.detail: Every inline style, every column and the `key={i.id}` came across unchanged from page.tsx lines 13-32. That is what lets app/invoices/page.test.tsx stay untouched and still pass, and it is what the second screenshot is there to show. If you read one thing in the diff, read that the <table> block is a move and not a rewrite.

focus.title: The new component takes the list as a prop, which is the only reason the empty branch is testable
focus.detail: page.tsx calls listInvoices() directly, and that returns a hard-coded five-invoice array — so a conditional inside the page could never be exercised without vi.mock of @/lib/invoices, a pattern this repo does not use. InvoiceTable takes `invoices: readonly Invoice[]`, so both branches are reachable with the plain render/DOM pattern already in components/ExportButton.test.tsx. Both files report 100% of lines.

focus.title: There is no status filter in this app yet — this is the empty state only
focus.detail: The request named a status filter as an example of when the table would be empty, not as the thing to build. Nothing here adds filtering; listInvoices() still returns every invoice. Adding the filter is issue #27. Consequently the empty state is not reachable through the UI today, which is why the proof for it comes from a temporary edit to the seed plus the unit test, rather than from clicking something.

focus.title: The sibling import is extensionless on purpose
focus.detail: page.tsx imports "./InvoiceTable", not "./InvoiceTable.js". The repo's convention is a .js extension for relative imports, and that is still correct in the test file — but Next's webpack resolver does not rewrite .js to .tsx for app source, so the .js form type-checks and passes vitest while failing `next build` with "Module not found". Please don't normalise it.
